title: API Knowledge Record
description: A single, agent-readable knowledge record about an API. Aggregates evidence from one or more sources (APIs.json, APIs.guru, RapidAPI, Postman, the provider's own portal, Naftiko Signals) into a structured, source-cited view of one API surface.

id.description: Stable, lowercase, dash-delimited identifier for the API knowledge record. Should be globally unique within the knowledge layer. Convention: '{provider-slug}:{api-slug}'.

description.description: One-paragraph description of what the API does, written from the provider's own materials.

humanURL.description: Canonical developer-portal URL for the API.

baseURL.description: Canonical request base URL for the API, if it has one.

provider.description: The organization or person operating the API.

capability.description: What the API can actually do. The agent-facing capability summary.

summary.description: One-line capability summary, e.g. 'Send SMS messages globally', 'Query U.S. census tracts by FIPS code'.

categories.description: Coarse categories the API belongs to (e.g. 'Communications', 'Payments', 'AI/ML').

sources.description: Every place where this API is described or indexed. At least one entry is required.

sourceOfTruth.description: URL identifying the authoritative source for this API (typically the provider's own OpenAPI or developer portal). Used when sources conflict.

artifacts.description: Machine-readable artifacts that describe this API.

signals.description: External signals attached to this API (GitHub stars, hiring activity, changelog cadence, Naftiko Signal groups, etc.).

confidence.description: Aggregate confidence in the record, derived from source diversity and recency.

type.description: Kind of source emitting this evidence.

url.description: URL of the source page or file.

retrieved.description: When this source was last verified.

evidence.description: A piece of cited evidence supporting a claim in the knowledge record.

quote.description: Verbatim quote from the source. Should be short enough to fall within fair use.

claim.description: The claim the quote supports (e.g. 'has public OpenAPI', 'rate limit 1000/hour', 'provider is a Linux Foundation member').

url.description: URL of the page the quote is from, if different from the parent source URL.

value.description: Signal value, untyped because signal types vary.
